scope.flow: Distributor._setClaimRecipient stores claimRecipient[user][token] = recipient but emits ClaimRecipientUpdated with arguments in an order that swaps the token and recipient topics relative to the declared event signature
scope.environment: on-chain Merkl Distributor contract; off-chain indexers, analytics pipelines and payout automation consuming the emitted event
evidence: `Distributor._setClaimRecipient` stores `claimRecipient[user][token] = recipient` but emits `ClaimRecipientUpdated(user, recipient, token)` while the event is declared as `(user, token, recipient)`. As a result, the log’s indexed `token` topic actually holds the recipient address and the `recipient` topic holds the token address. Off-chain indexers that rebuild `claimRecipient` from events will construct the inverse mapping and surface incorrect recipient/token pairs.

The mismatch is visible in the event declaration at [`contracts/Distributor.sol:119-120`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-merkl/blob/main/contracts/Distributor.sol#L119-L120) and the emit site at [`contracts/Distributor.sol:540-546`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-merkl/blob/main/contracts/Distributor.sol#L540-L546):
- [`contracts/Distributor.sol:119-120`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-merkl/blob/main/contracts/Distributor.sol#L119-L120) event parameter order `(user, token, recipient)`
- [`contracts/Distributor.sol:540-546`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-merkl/blob/main/contracts/Distributor.sol#L540-L546) emit passes `(user, recipient, token)`, swapping topics

ambiguities: No attacker, authorization or permissionless-call condition is described; the scenario involves a contract-internal event-emission mismatch.
No concrete submitted transaction, user or token values are provided, so the described state is a possible scenario rather than an observed incident.
Whether any actual off-chain payout was misrouted is reported as potential (will/can), not as an asserted loss.
